_comment: Issue #44: every wave-B RAM variable whose unit or scaling one logging
session turns from VERIFIED-STATIC into VERIFIED-DYNAMIC, plus the three
raster activation counters whose slopes settle the task periods of
re/findings/scheduler.md (see the corrected note below).
26 variables in 17 DDLI chunks (the logger merges adjacent addresses),
56 bytes per record -- inside the 20-chunk limit of dynamic id 0xF0
(re/findings/kwp.md section 4.1).  No SecurityAccess needed: session 0x89,
2C F0 03 ..., then 21 F0 as fast as the bus allows.
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/wave_b_confirm.json \
--bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 70 -o logs/2026-xx-xx_wave_b.csv
Scenario (same as patches/ff_counter/test/procedure.md section 3):
0-30 s idle, 30-40 s one load step, 40-70 s idle, engine warm.
RASTER COUNTERS -- CORRECTED 2026-09-16 from brief C4
(re/findings/scheduler.md sections 11-12, agent/C4, being merged).
Brief C3 first wrote these as the 10 / 20 / 100 ms counters, following
scheduler.md section 5.4.  C4 measured the OS time base: 1 ms = 3508 Time
Base ticks of 285 ns, not 701.754, so the periods in section 5.4 were all
too long.  The corrected periods are below, and they are what this file
logs.
The firmware also carries TWO task sets and only one is live: os_init
installs set A, and 0x11DA64 switches to set B if 0x7FEB5E != 0.  The two
set-A cells are logged as well, so a frozen set-B counter can be told
apart from a broken logger: exactly one of the two sets must be counting.
addr        set  period   expected slope
0x7FD75C    A      1 ms   +1000/s
Expect every rate to come out about 0.25 % LOW: the OS truncates the
285.714 ns tick to 285 ns, so its millisecond is slightly long.  A 0.25 %
deviation confirms the model; a 5x or 10x one does not.

vars.name: dwkrz_1
vars.notes: knock retard, measuring ids 88-93, formula 0x22 A=0x4B -> (B-128)*0.75. Cylinder order COMMUNITY.

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: set A 10 ms epilogue counter; expect +100/s if set A is live, frozen if set B is

vars.name: raster_setB_10ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 10 ms epilogue counter (0x120570, the task C1's Flash-1 hook sits in); expect +100/s

vars.name: raster_setA_1ms_count
vars.notes: set A 1 ms epilogue counter; expect +1000/s if set A is live

vars.name: raster_setB_1ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 1 ms epilogue counter (0x11EBDC); expect +1000/s -- the fastest reference

vars.name: raster_setB_2ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 2 ms epilogue counter (0x11ED50); expect +500/s

vars.name: zwist_display_b1
vars.source: re/findings/ignition.md; measuring id 9, VCDS group 003 field 4

vars.name: tmot_w
vars.notes: u16, 0.75/256 degC per LSB; tmot is its high byte

vars.name: ksta_adapted
vars.notes: ksta * kstaa, 1024 = 1.0; outside the start it is pinned at 1.0

vars.name: rk_fuel_mass
vars.notes: relative fuel mass, u16; the LSB value is not settled

vars.name: dwi_inj_angle
vars.notes: same 3/128 degCA unit as wbho1s_w, which it is compared against

vars.name: ti_sum
vars.notes: u32, 1 us per LSB; VCDS group 002 field 3

vars.name: vmsv_limited
vars.notes: pinned at 5000 means the high-pressure pump is saturated

vars.name: vhdp_spare
vars.notes: (VHDPMX 25120 - vhdp_dem) * 0.1; zero means the pump is at its limit
